title_en: Xinda Company, Hefei Office v. China National Pharmaceutical Group Corporation et al. — dispute over a loan guarantee contract

full_text_en:
Xinda Company Hefei Office v. China Pharmaceutical Group Corporation et al. — Dispute over Loan Guarantee Contract

[Ruling Summary]

After a change in the property rights relationship of an enterprise due to the overall transfer of all its assets, if the enterprise that receives the assets without compensation contributes all the operational net assets and corresponding debts of the received enterprise as its own capital contribution to form a new subsidiary, it shall bear joint and several liability for the original debts of the received enterprise within the scope of the assets it accepted.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2004) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 54

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Huainan No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory. Address: Guoqing West Road, Huainan City, Anhui Province.
Legal Representative: Yang Xiufang, Factory Director.
Agent ad litem: Li Chaoding, Lawyer at Beijing Zhongkai Law Firm.

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): China Pharmaceutical Group Corporation. Address: No. 20 Zhichun Road, Haidian District, Beijing.
Legal Representative: Zheng Hong, Chairman of the Board.
Agent ad litem: Xing Yonggang, Employee of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Wang Zongyu, Lawyer at Beijing Dishi Law Firm.

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance): China Cinda Asset Management Corporation, Hefei Office. Address: Run'an Building, No. 166 Funan Road, Hefei City, Anhui Province.
Person in Charge: Ji Deqin, Office Director.
Agent ad litem: Wang Xiuye, Manager of the Office.
Agent ad litem: Wang Yanling, Lawyer at Beijing Tiantong Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Huainan Wanhuai Chemical Factory. Address: Tiandong Road, Tianjiao'an District, Huainan City, Anhui Province.
Legal Representative: Hu Qiang, Factory Director.
Agent ad litem: Song Ming, Employee of the Factory.
Agent ad litem: Yang Zhongjing, Employee of the Factory.

The appellants, Huainan No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory (hereinafter referred to as No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory) and China Pharmaceutical Group Corporation (hereinafter referred to as Pharmaceutical Group Corporation), appealed to this Court against the civil judgment (2003) Wan Min Er Chu Zi No. 7 rendered by the Anhui High People's Court in the dispute over loan guarantee contract with the respondents, China Cinda Asset Management Corporation, Hefei Office (hereinafter referred to as Cinda Hefei Office) and Huainan Wanhuai Chemical Factory (hereinafter referred to as Chemical Factory). This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel composed of Presiding Judge Fu Jinlian, Judge Jin Jianfeng, and Acting Judge Li Jingping for trial, with Zhang Xuemei serving as court clerk. The case is now concluded.

The court of first instance found the following facts:

On December 16, 1996, the Chemical Factory entered into a loan contract with the China Development Bank (hereinafter referred to as CDB). The contract stipulated that the Chemical Factory would borrow RMB 10.28 million from the CDB for the purpose of the overall drainage comprehensive treatment project of the Chemical Factory. The loan term was 5 years, i.e., from December 1996 to December 2001, with the loan interest rate calculated at 11.70% per annum, payable quarterly. Unpaid interest at maturity would be subject to compound interest. During the effective period of the contract, if the interest rate was adjusted, it would be implemented according to the provisions of the People's Bank of China. The Chemical Factory guaranteed to repay the loan according to the following installment repayment plan within the loan term: RMB 2 million before December 20, 1999; RMB 3 million before December 20, 2000; and RMB 5.28 million before December 20, 2001. The CDB entrusted the Huainan Sub-branch of the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China as the agent bank to handle the disbursement of the loan funds. On December 12, 1996, the CDB and No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory signed a guarantee contract. The contract stipulated that No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory would provide a guarantee for the principal of RMB 10.28 million, interest, and related expenses to the CDB, with the guarantee method being joint and several liability for repayment, and the guarantee period commencing from the effective date of the main contract until its termination. After the contract became effective, if the CDB and the Chemical Factory needed to amend the terms of the main contract, they should obtain the consent of No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory, and a written agreement should be signed by the three parties: No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory, the CDB, and the Chemical Factory. After the loan contract and guarantee contract were signed, the CDB disbursed the loan in the same month. Upon the expiration of the repayment term stipulated in the contract, the Chemical Factory failed to perform its repayment obligations, and No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory also failed to perform its guarantee obligations.

On December 26, 1999, the CDB and Cinda Hefei Office signed a "Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement," stipulating that the CDB's creditor's rights against the Chemical Factory, consisting of the principal loan balance of RMB 10.28 million and accrued but unpaid interest of RMB 1,875,538.01 as of December 20, 1999, totaling RMB 12,155,538.01, were transferred to Cinda Hefei Office. On December 21, 1999, the CDB sent a notice of creditor's rights transfer to the Chemical Factory, informing it that the creditor's rights under the contract had been transferred to Cinda Hefei Office, and the Chemical Factory confirmed by affixing its seal on the receipt of the transfer notice. On January 19, 2000, the CDB published an announcement in Anhui Daily, notifying the Chemical Factory and No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory of the transfer of creditor's rights and the transfer of guarantee rights.

On December 31, 1997, the Chemical Factory signed two loan contracts with the Huainan Sub-branch of China Construction Bank, with loan amounts of RMB 500,000 and RMB 8.24 million, respectively. The loan purposes were technical transformation and production turnover. The loan term was from December 23, 1997, to October 22, 2000, with interest calculated at a monthly rate of 8.19‰, payable quarterly. After the above contracts were signed, the Huainan Sub-branch of China Construction Bank fulfilled its lending obligations as agreed. Upon the expiration of the loan contracts, the Chemical Factory failed to perform its repayment obligations. On November 18, 1999, the Huainan Branch of China Construction Bank and Cinda Hefei Office signed a "Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement," transferring the creditor's rights for the principal and interest of the above two loans, totaling RMB 9,341,482.44, to Cinda Hefei Office. On November 8, 1999, the Huainan Branch of China Construction Bank sent a notice of creditor's rights transfer to the Chemical Factory, and the Chemical Factory confirmed by affixing its seal on the receipt of the creditor's rights transfer notice.

On July 12, 2001, Cinda Hefei Office issued a notice of loan collection and a notice of performance of guarantee obligations to the Chemical Factory and No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory for the above three loans. On July 31, 2001, the Chemical Factory and No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory respectively confirmed by affixing their seals on the receipts of the notices. On June 19, 2003, Cinda Hefei Office published a creditor's rights collection announcement in Anhui Legal News, requesting the debtor Chemical Factory and the guarantor No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory to immediately perform the obligation to repay the matured debts.

Additionally, it was found that on November 18, 1997, the Huainan Municipal People's Government, by document Huai Fu Mi (1997) No. 154, agreed that all assets of No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory would be transferred to China Pharmaceutical (Group) Company through an overall allocation, making it a wholly-owned subsidiary of China Pharmaceutical (Group) Company. On April 19, 1998, the State Pharmaceutical Administration, by document Guo Yao Guan Ban (1998) No. 19, approved that China Pharmaceutical (Group) Company would receive No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory through an overall allocation of state-owned assets, making it a wholly-owned subsidiary of China Pharmaceutical (Group) Company. Upon capital verification, as of July 31, 1998, the total assets of No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory were RMB 79,605,196.08, and the net assets were RMB 28,031,450.17. Additionally, according to the asset appraisal report commissioned by the Pharmaceutical Group Corporation, the Pharmaceutical Group Corporation had contributed the operational assets of No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory as its capital investment to a newly established enterprise. In November 1998, China Pharmaceutical (Group) Company, after being separated from central government-affiliated enterprises and government departments, changed its name to Pharmaceutical Group Corporation.

Cinda Hefei Office filed a lawsuit with the court of first instance on August 11, 2003, requesting a judgment ordering the Chemical Factory to repay the loan principal of RMB 19.02 million and interest of RMB 11,397,614.46; ordering No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory to bear joint and several liability for repayment of the principal of RMB 10.28 million and interest of RMB 5,113,121.30; ordering the Pharmaceutical Group Corporation to bear liability for repayment within the scope of No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory's joint and several guarantee liability; and ordering the above defendants to bear the litigation costs of this case.

The court of first instance held that: The loan contract and guarantee contract signed between the CDB and the Chemical Factory and No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory, as well as the loan contracts signed between the Huainan Sub-branch of China Construction Bank and the Chemical Factory, had legal subject qualifications for all parties, the parties' expressions of intention were genuine, and they complied with legal provisions. Therefore, the above loan contracts and guarantee contract were legally valid. All parties should perform their obligations according to the contract, and the breaching party should bear liability for breach of contract. In accordance with the State Council's policy on the剥离 of non-performing assets from state-owned banks and the relevant provisions of the People's Bank of China and the Ministry of Finance, the "Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement" signed between the CDB and Cinda Hefei Office neither changed the content of the original contract nor increased the guarantee liability of the guarantor No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory. Moreover, in the guarantee contract, No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory did not agree with the CDB to prohibit the transfer of creditor's rights or promise to assume guarantee liability only to the CDB. Therefore, the defense of the Pharmaceutical Group Corporation that No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory would no longer bear guarantee liability because the creditor's rights transfer was not agreed to by No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory lacked factual and legal basis, and the court did not support it. After Cinda Hefei Office received the creditor's rights under the three loan contracts, it issued a notice of loan collection to the Chemical Factory on July 12, 2001, and the Chemical Factory signed and confirmed receipt of the collection notice, causing the statute of limitations to be interrupted. On June 19, 2003, Cinda Hefei Office published an announcement in Anhui Legal News to collect the creditor's rights from the Chemical Factory, again causing the statute of limitations to be interrupted. The Chemical Factory argued that the publication of an announcement by a financial asset management company does not constitute an interruption of the statute of limitations. According to the opinion of the Supreme People's Court in the "Letter on the Implementation of the Supreme People's Court's 'Twelve Articles' Judicial Interpretation," a financial asset management company may obtain evidence of statute of limitations interruption by publishing a collection announcement in a nationwide or provincial influential newspaper. The announcement containing the content of creditor's rights collection published by Cinda Hefei Office in Anhui Legal News on June 19, 2003, lawfully constituted evidence of statute of limitations interruption. Therefore, the Chemical Factory's defense that part of Cinda Hefei Office's creditor's rights had exceeded the statute of limitations was untenable, and the court did not accept it. After No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory provided a guarantee for the loan contract signed between the Chemical Factory and the CDB, it confirmed by affixing its seal on the notice of performance of guarantee obligations issued by Cinda Hefei Office on July 31, 2001. Therefore, No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory should bear guarantee liability for the Chemical Factory's debts. The claims of the Pharmaceutical Group Corporation and No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory that the provision of the guarantee was not the true intention of No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory and constituted an invalid civil act lacked factual basis, and the court did not accept them. The loan contract stipulated that the Chemical Factory would repay the borrowed funds in installments, but at the same time, the contract stipulated the performance period, which meant that the rights and obligations under the contract were indivisible. Since the guarantee contract did not stipulate a guarantee period, the period for No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory to assume guarantee liability in this case should be determined as two years from the date of maturity of the main debt, i.e., from December 2001 to December 2003. The publication of the creditor's rights collection announcement by Cinda Hefei Office in Anhui Legal News on June 19, 2003, did not exceed the guarantee period. Cinda Hefei Office's assertion of its rights against the joint and several liability guarantor No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory within the statutory guarantee period complied with legal provisions, and the court supported it. According to document Huai Fu Mi (1997) No. 154 of the Huainan Municipal People's Government and document Guo Yao Guan Ban (1998) No. 19 of the State Pharmaceutical Administration, No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory had been fully incorporated into the Pharmaceutical Group Corporation. The assets of an enterprise are both the material basis for its business operations and its general guarantee for assuming civil liability to the outside world. The Pharmaceutical Group Corporation received the assets of No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory without compensation. Without handling the original debts of No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory and without obtaining the prior consent or subsequent approval of the creditors, it actually disposed of its assets, resulting in a reduction of No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory's capacity to assume civil liability to the outside world. Based on the principle that the debts of an enterprise follow changes in its assets, Cinda Hefei Office requested that the Pharmaceutical Group Corporation assume civil liability within the scope of the assets it received, which had a legal basis, and the court supported it. In summary, in accordance with Articles 6 and 40(1)(2) of the Economic Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 18 and 31 of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 28 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China, and Articles 128 and 138 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the court rendered the following judgment: 1. The Chemical Factory shall, within ten days after this judgment takes effect, repay Cinda Hefei Office the loan principal of RMB 19.02 million and interest of RMB 11,397,614.46 (interest calculated up to June 21, 2003; thereafter, interest shall be calculated in accordance with the standard for overdue loan interest stipulated by the People's Bank of China until the date of actual payment); 2. No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory shall bear joint and several liability for repayment of the principal of RMB 10.28 million and interest of RMB 5,113,121.30 within the loan principal and interest that the Chemical Factory should repay to Cinda Hefei Office under item 1 of this judgment. After assuming joint and several liability for repayment, No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory has the right to seek recourse from the Chemical Factory; 3. The Pharmaceutical Group Corporation shall bear joint and several liability for the above debts of No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory within the scope of the assets it received. The case acceptance fee of RMB 97,259 shall be borne by the Chemical Factory.

Both No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory and China Pharmaceutical Group Corporation were dissatisfied with the above civil judgment of the court of first instance and filed appeals to this Court.

No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory appealed alleging: 1. The guarantee contract signed between No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory and the original creditor bank and the Chemical Factory was not the true intention of No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory, but rather the result of pressure and compulsion imposed on No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory by the original creditor bank and the Chemical Factory through the municipal government, violating the mandatory provisions of Article 11 of the Guarantee Law and should be deemed an invalid civil act. 2. Although the guarantee contract signed between No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory, the original creditor bank, and the Chemical Factory did not expressly stipulate "only assume guarantee liability to a specific creditor" or "prohibit transfer of creditor's rights," its Articles 5 and 13 clearly stated that any changes must be agreed to by No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory and confirmed by a written agreement signed by the three parties. No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory's guarantee was directed at the China Development Bank. If the China Development Bank intended to change the creditor, it must obtain the written consent of No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory. However, in fact, the original creditor bank violated the contract by unilaterally changing the main creditor, and therefore No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory should naturally no longer bear guarantee liability. 3. The original judgment disregarded the specific installment repayment periods stipulated in the loan contract for the Chemical Factory's repayment of the borrowed funds, and only took the repayment date of December 20, 2001, for the last installment of RMB 5.28 million out of the total loan of RMB 10.28 million as the performance period of the contract, thereby determining the date of maturity of the Chemical Factory's main debt. The conclusion that the period for No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory to assume guarantee liability was based on this was untenable. During the period from July 12, 2001, to July 12, 2003, Cinda Hefei Office neither filed a lawsuit with the court nor asserted its rights against No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory; it only published a so-called "collection announcement" in Anhui Legal News on June 19, 2003. However, Anhui Legal News is only a "weekly newspaper" and is not considered an "influential" newspaper among provincial-level newspapers. Therefore, this act cannot constitute evidence of statute of limitations interruption.

Pharmaceutical Group Corporation appealed alleging: 1. The judgment of first instance did not confirm the fact that the guarantee contract signed between the CDB and No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory on December 12, 1996, was the result of compulsion by the Huainan municipal government department. The guarantee contract should be deemed invalid. The court of first instance's judgment that No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory should bear guarantee liability lacked legal basis. No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory assumed guarantee liability only towards the specific creditor, the CDB. However, when the original creditor bank transferred its creditor's rights against the Chemical Factory to Cinda Hefei Office, a significant change in the contract subject occurred without obtaining the consent of No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory, and no written agreement was reached among the parties. In accordance with the law, No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory should no longer bear guarantee liability. 2. The judgment of first instance failed to determine the specific amount of assets received by the Pharmaceutical Group Corporation from No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory and the specific amount of "operational assets" of No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory that the Pharmaceutical Group Corporation invested in other enterprises. The "Asset Transfer Agreement" signed between the Pharmaceutical Group Corporation and the Huainan Municipal Government only changed the subordinate relationship of No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory; the independent legal person status of No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory remained unchanged, and it should perform its obligations and assume liability with its own property in accordance with the law. The judgment of first instance requiring the Pharmaceutical Group Corporation, as the superior supervisory unit, to assume the guarantee liability of No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory lacked legal basis. Joint and several liability can only be established if there is a legal provision or agreement between the parties. There was no legal relationship between the Pharmaceutical Group Corporation and Cinda Hefei Office, and the judgment of first instance requiring the Pharmaceutical Group Corporation to assume joint and several liability had no legal basis. 3. The judgment of first instance failed to confirm the fact that Cinda Hefei Office's claims had exceeded the statute of limitations. 4. The transfer of property between the appellant and No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory was a governmental act, not an enterprise act. At the time of the transfer, no debts were transferred to the Pharmaceutical Group Corporation. Moreover, if other issues arise from the receipt of property, they should be resolved through other channels, rather than directly requiring the appellant to assume joint and several liability.

Respondent Cinda Hefei Office replied: 1. The guarantee contract in this case is valid. The guarantee contract signed by No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory as the guarantor on December 12, 1996, represented the true intentions of all parties, complied with legal provisions, and its validity is beyond doubt. The appellant's claim that the guarantee contract was the result of government directives and thus invalid due to violation of mandatory legal provisions lacks sufficient evidence. 2. The transfer of creditor's rights in this case is valid, and No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory should bear guarantee liability in accordance with the law. After Cinda Hefei Office and the CDB signed the "Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement," both Cinda Hefei Office and the CDB notified No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory and the Chemical Factory of the fact of the creditor's rights transfer, and No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory and the Chemical Factory confirmed by affixing their seals on the receipt of the relevant notices on July 31, 2001. Pursuant to Article 81 of the Contract Law and Article 28 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law, No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory should bear joint and several liability for repayment of the debts in this case. 3. There is no situation in this case where the guarantor is exempted due to the statute of limitations. According to the provisions of the Supreme People's Court, a financial asset management company may obtain evidence of statute of limitations interruption by publishing a collection announcement in a nationwide or provincial influential newspaper. Anhui Legal News is sponsored by the Anhui Provincial Committee of Political and Legal Affairs, with a circulation of 260,000 copies, demonstrating its influence among provincial newspapers in Anhui. Other asset management companies also choose to publish relevant announcements in this newspaper when collecting transferred creditor's rights. Additionally, the Supreme People's Court's judicial interpretation provides that in loan contracts, where the parties agree to perform the debt in installments, the statute of limitations shall commence from the day after the maturity date of the last installment. Therefore, the creditor's rights in this case have not exceeded the statute of limitations. 4. The Pharmaceutical Group Corporation should bear joint and several liability for the debts in this case within the scope of disposing of the assets of No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory. The Pharmaceutical Group Corporation received No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory without compensation around 1999, making it a wholly-owned subsidiary. After receiving No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory without compensation, the Pharmaceutical Group Corporation contributed all the operational net assets and liabilities of No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory as its capital investment to China National Pharmaceutical Group Corporation Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. in 1999, effectively disposing of the assets of No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory. The Pharmaceutical Group Corporation's act of disposing of the assets of No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory constitutes a tort against its legal person property rights and should bear corresponding legal liability.

The Appellee, the Chemical Plant, did not submit a written defense opinion. During the second instance cross-examination, it orally defended, stating: The guarantee contract existed as a matter of fact, and Xinda Hefei Office claimed the creditor's rights within the guarantee period and the statute of limitations period, requesting the court of second instance to render a judgment based on the facts.

Facts Found by the Court: On December 12, 1996, the Development Bank and No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory entered into a guarantee contract, which stipulated that No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory agreed to provide a guarantee to the Development Bank for the principal amount of RMB 10.28 million, plus interest and related expenses, with the guarantee method being joint and several liability for repayment, and the guarantee period commencing from the effective date of the principal contract until its expiration. On December 26, 1999, the Development Bank and Xinda Hefei Office executed the "Creditor's Rights Assignment Agreement," assigning the creditor's rights under the aforementioned loan contract to Xinda Hefei Office, and issued a notice of assignment of creditor's rights to the Chemical Plant, which acknowledged by affixing its seal on the receipt of the assignment notice. On January 19, 2000, the Development Bank published a public notice in Anhui Daily notifying the Chemical Plant and No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory of the assignment of creditor's rights and the transfer of security rights. In November 1997, pursuant to relevant documents from the Huainan Municipal People's Government and the State Drug Administration, all assets of No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory were transferred in their entirety to the Pharmaceutical Group Company, and No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory became a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Pharmaceutical Group Company. In 1999, with the Pharmaceutical Group Company as the sponsor, Sinopharm Group Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. was established, whereby all of No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory's appraised and confirmed net operating assets and corresponding liabilities were contributed as the Pharmaceutical Group Company's capital contribution to Sinopharm Group Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.

Opinion of the Court: The loan contract concluded between the Development Bank and the Chemical Plant, and the guarantee contract concluded between the Development Bank and No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory, are legal and valid. The Chemical Plant shall perform its repayment obligations in accordance with the terms of the loan contract, and No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory shall assume the guarantee liability in accordance with the guarantee contract. The Appellants, No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory and the Pharmaceutical Group Company, argued that the guarantee contract was provided under government directives and was invalid due to violation of mandatory legal provisions. However, this argument lacks sufficient evidence, and moreover, after the execution of the guarantee contract and before the dispute arose, the guarantor, No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory, did not promptly seek to revoke the contract. The ground of appeal by No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory and the Pharmaceutical Group Company, that providing the guarantee was not the true intention of No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory and constituted a void civil act, lacks factual basis, and this Court does not uphold it.

The Development Bank and Xinda Hefei Office executed the "Creditor's Rights Assignment Agreement," assigning the creditor's rights under the aforementioned loan contract to Xinda Hefei Office, and issued a notice of assignment of creditor's rights to the Chemical Plant, which acknowledged by affixing its seal on the receipt of the assignment notice. The loan contract in this case stipulated that the Chemical Plant should perform its repayment obligations in installments for the borrowed funds, and the loan contract explicitly specified the performance period for all debts. Accordingly, the rights and obligations under the loan contract are indivisible. At the same time, the guarantee contract did not stipulate a guarantee period. Therefore, the guarantee period during which No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory assumed the guarantee liability shall be determined as two years from the date the principal debt performance period expired, i.e., from December 2001 to December 2003. After Xinda Hefei Office accepted the creditor's rights under the loan contract, the Chemical Plant and No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory, on July 31, 2001, acknowledged by affixing their seals on the notice of debt collection and the notice of performance of guarantee obligations issued by Xinda Hefei Office. Xinda Hefei Office published a notice of debt collection in Anhui Legal Daily on June 19, 2003, which did not exceed the guarantee period. Therefore, No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory shall assume the guarantee liability for the debts of the Chemical Plant. The grounds of appeal by the Appellants, No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory and the Pharmaceutical Group Company, that No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory no longer bears guarantee liability because the assignment of creditor's rights was not consented to by No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory, and that Xinda Hefei Office did not assert its rights against No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory within the guarantee period and the statute of limitations period, cannot be established, and this Court does not uphold them.

According to Document No. Huai Fu Mi (1997) No. 154 of the Huainan Municipal People's Government and Document No. Guo Yao Guan Ban (1998) No. 19 of the State Drug Administration, all assets of No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory were transferred in their entirety to the Pharmaceutical Group Company, and No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory became a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Pharmaceutical Group Company. In 1999, with the Pharmaceutical Group Company as the sponsor, Sinopharm Group Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. was established, whereby all of No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory's appraised and confirmed net operating assets and corresponding liabilities were contributed as the Pharmaceutical Group Company's capital contribution to Sinopharm Group Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., which in effect disposed of the assets of No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory. The above facts are confirmed by evidence including the "Prospectus" of Sinopharm Group Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., the "Capital Verification Report" of Beijing Jingdu Certified Public Accountants Co., Ltd., and the "Letter on the Review Opinions of the Asset Appraisal Project for the Proposed Establishment of a Pharmaceutical Joint-Stock Company by the Pharmaceutical Group Company and Other Units" from the Ministry of Finance, and can be established. All of No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory's net operating assets were contributed by the Pharmaceutical Group Company to Sinopharm Group Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., but the shareholder's rights and interests were not enjoyed by No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory in accordance with the law; instead, they were enjoyed by the Pharmaceutical Group Company. The Pharmaceutical Group Company accepted the assets of No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory without compensation, and without addressing the original debts of No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory and without obtaining prior consent or subsequent ratification from the creditors, it disposed of the assets of No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory. Therefore, the original judgment ordering the Pharmaceutical Group Company to assume joint and several liability for repayment of the debts of No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory to the extent of the assets it accepted is not improper. The ground of appeal by the Appellant, the Pharmaceutical Group Company, that "No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory's status as an independent legal person has not changed and should perform its obligations and assume responsibility with its own property in accordance with the law" cannot be established, and this Court does not uphold it. The court of first instance found the facts clearly, had sufficient evidence, and correctly applied the law. In accordance with Article 153, Paragraph 1, Subparagraph (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court hereby renders the following judgment:

Appeal dismissed and the original judgment affirmed.

Court costs for the second instance in the amount of RMB 194,518 shall be borne by Huainan No. 6 Pharmaceutical Factory in the amount of RMB 97,259 and by China National Pharmaceutical Group Corporation in the amount of RMB 97,259.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Fu Jinlian

Judge: Jin Jianfeng

Acting Judge: Li Jingping

September 13, 2004

Clerk: Zhang Xuemei

[Profile of the Presiding Judge]

Fu Jinlian, Senior Judge: Born in 1964, Master of Laws. Appointed as a Judge of the Supreme People's Court in 1996.
